answer.answer: Visa states that the interchange multidistrict litigation involves complaints filed by merchants against Visa U.S.A., Visa International, Mastercard, and certain U.S. financial institutions, which were transferred to the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York for pre-trial proceedings in MDL 1720 [1][2]. These complaints challenge items such as interchange reimbursement fees, "no surcharge" and honor-all-cards rules, alleged tying and bundling of transaction fees, and Visa's reorganization and IPO under federal antitrust and state unfair competition laws [1]. During fiscal 2025, Visa recorded additional accruals of $2.2 billion and deposited $875 million into the U.S. litigation escrow account to address claims associated with this litigation [3][4]. As of September 30, 2025, the company recorded a litigation accrual of $2,698 million for the Interchange Multidistrict Litigation - Individual Merchant Actions [5]. Visa's board of directors will consider continued resolution in the interchange multidistrict litigation regarding successive exchange offers for class B common stock [4].
